questions.question: What is outage?

options.text: It is only a concern in warm weather.
It is the same for every liquid.
It should be considered when deciding how much liquid to put in a tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be considered when deciding how much liquid to put in a tank.
questions.explanation: Liquids expand when they get hot. You must leave space in the tank for this expansion. This space is called "outage." Different liquids need different amounts of outage.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you start driving. If you have a trailer, make sure it is straight so you can adjust the mirrors correctly.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Always downshift before you enter a curve.

questions.question: What should you do if your trailer drifts while backing?

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, turn the steering wheel in the direction of the drift to correct it right away.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly toward the floor.
Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it moves, there may be a leak or another problem in the braking system.

questions.question: How much should you reduce your speed on packed snow?
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving on surfaces with less grip. On packed snow, reduce your speed by one-half or more.

questions.question: Are wheels with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if a professional did the repairs.
Yes, if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Do not use wheels or rims that have been welded. Replace them before driving on the road.

questions.question: What should happen when you start from a stop?

options.text: The vehicle should shift to the right.
The vehicle should be in third gear.
The vehicle should not roll backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.

questions.question: What is true about driving a tank vehicle with liquid cargo?

options.text: It is not allowed during normal business hours.
It is harder than driving a tank vehicle with solid cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder than driving a tank vehicle with solid cargo.
questions.explanation: Driving a tank vehicle with liquid cargo is harder because tanks sit high and liquid cargo can surge. The movement of liquid inside can make the vehicle unstable.

questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, how far ahead should you watch the road?
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead to see obstacles and hazards. At highway speeds, this equals about a quarter mile.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles, you must:
questions.explanation: Some vehicles require the engine to be running when you check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If an air supply control is in the "emergency" position:

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
More air will go to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. If an air supply control is set to "emergency", the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes are applied.

questions.question: While the vehicle is running, vents should:
questions.explanation: Before driving a tank, check that vents and manhole covers have gaskets and close properly. Keep vents clear so they work correctly.

questions.question: What should you do if the braking system will not build pressure?

options.text: Press the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes will not build enough pressure to slow or stop the vehicle, try shifting to a lower gear, pumping the brakes, or using the emergency brake.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be repaired, but it can wait.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and load while keeping the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be fixed immediately.

questions.question: Engine belts should:
questions.explanation: When checking your engine, look at the belts for tightness and wear. How much movement is safe depends on your specific vehicle, so learn what is right for yours.

questions.question: When you start the engine:

options.text: Warning lights should come on, then go off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should come on, then go off quickly.
questions.explanation: When the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, there may be a problem with the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Not use your mirrors in heavy traffic.
Look only ahead and to the right.
Look ahead, to the sides, and behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead, to the sides, and behind.
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Check the road ahead and use both mirrors regularly while driving.
